findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The key `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian (lt) account message bundle was changed from a Lithuanian sentence to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users of the account console will see an Italian instruction during TOTP setup. This looks like the English source text ('Install one of the following applications on your mobile:') was machine-translated into the wrong target language. It should be replaced with an actual Lithuanian translation.

findings.title: Lithuanian login translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The key `loginTotpStep1` in the Lithuanian (lt) login message bundle was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see Italian text on the TOTP setup page of the login flow. It should be a Lithuanian translation of 'Install one of the following applications on your mobile:'.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) message replaced with Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: The key `totpStep1` in the zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) account bundle was changed to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 安裝, 應用程式) while the rest of the file is Simplified Chinese (compare the login zh_CN file, which uses `在您的移动设备中安装以下任意一个应用：` for the same message). Simplified-Chinese users will see inconsistent, effectively wrong-locale text on the TOTP setup page.

findings.title: Email-file detection uses fragile substring match on file path
findings.body: `normalizeValue` strips ` style="direction: rtl;"` whenever `file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email")` is true. This matches any directory or file name containing the substring 'email' anywhere in the path (e.g., a theme directory named 'emails' or a custom path containing 'email'), not just the intended `theme/base/email/messages` location. In such a case the verifier would silently normalize away a legitimate style attribute and hide a real HTML mismatch. The check should match the path segment explicitly (e.g., a regex on `theme/base/email/` or a path component equals 'email').
